why: Var = (sum of squares)/n - mean^2 = 48/4 - 9 = 3 exactly, so the standard deviation is sqrt(3). Verified with exact rational arithmetic.

The data is an AP with d=7, n=7, mean 30; deviations are -21..21 giving sum of squares 1372 and population variance 196, so SD = 14. (The sample SD with n-1 would be 7*sqrt(42)/3 = 15.12, which matches no option, so the population SD is intended.)

Writing c = cos^2 x the equation becomes 9c^2 + 12c - 5 = 0, whose only admissible root is c = 1/3; then cos 2x = 2c-1 = -1/3 and cos 4x = 2cos^2 2x - 1 = -7/9. The stem as printed is consistent and was checked numerically at 40 dps (LHS = RHS = 8.3333...).

value: tan 1 deg + tan 89 deg = 1/(sin1 cos1) = 2/sin 2 deg = 57.3074166956876...
why: tan 89 deg = cot 1 deg, so the sum is (sin^2+cos^2)/(sin1 cos1) = 1/(sin1 cos1) = 2/sin2 deg exactly. Option C (1/sin 1 deg = 57.29868...) is a deliberate near-miss decoy differing only in the 3rd decimal, so this was discriminated at 50 dps: the value matches A to 1e-47 and differs from C by 0.00873.

3 tan x = 4 tan y cross-multiplies to 4 sin y cos x = 3 sin x cos y = 3/4, so sin y cos x = 3/16; then sin(x-y) = sin x cos y - cos x sin y = 1/4 - 3/16 = 1/16. Confirmed by nsolve-ing an actual pair (x,y) satisfying both given constraints and evaluating sin(x-y) = 0.0625.

cos(5pi/8) = -cos(3pi/8) and cos(7pi/8) = -cos(pi/8), so the product pairs into (1-cos^2 pi/8)(1-cos^2 3pi/8) = sin^2(pi/8) sin^2(3pi/8) = sin^2(pi/8)cos^2(pi/8) = 1/8. sympy gives the exact value 1/8; the four options are numerically distinct (0.5, 0.9239, 0.125, 0.8536).

pi/12 and 5pi/12 are complementary, so cos^2(pi/12) + cos^2(5pi/12) = cos^2(15deg) + sin^2(15deg) = 1, plus cos^2(pi/4) = 1/2, giving 3/2. sympy simplifies the expression to exactly 3/2 and the other three options are numerically distinct.

tan b + cot b = 2/sin 2b, so the condition is 2/cos 2a = 2/sin 2b, i.e. sin 2b = cos 2a = sin(pi/2 - 2a), giving 2b = pi/2 - 2a and alpha + beta = pi/4. Checked numerically for alpha = 5, 10, 20, 35 deg: the equation holds to 1e-30 in every case and alpha+beta = 45.000000 deg each time. (The supplementary branch instead fixes beta - alpha = pi/4, so pi/4 is the intended principal answer.)

Pairing gives 4 cos(5x/2) cos x cos(x/2) = 0, so cos(5x/2)=0 (5 roots), cos x = 0 (2 roots) and cos(x/2)=0 (x=pi, already counted), i.e. 7 distinct roots. Confirmed by a 200,000-point bracketed root scan over [0,2pi) which found exactly 7 roots, each residual < 1e-34.

value: cos 2x = 0, i.e. x = (2n+1)pi/4; option A (2n pi +/- pi/4) is a valid but PROPER SUBSET of that set
why: The equation factors as cos 2x (2 cos x + 1) = 0 and the restriction cos x != -1/2 kills the second factor, leaving cos 2x = 0, i.e. x = pi/4 + n pi/2. Every value in option A satisfies the equation (residual ~1e-41) while every value in B, C and D fails outright (f = -1, 1.366, -1), so A is the only defensible letter. Recorded as a genuine option defect rather than a wrong key: A omits the branches 3pi/4 and 5pi/4, which satisfy the equation with cos x = -0.7071 (not the excluded -1/2); the complete set needs 'n pi/2 + pi/4' or '(2n+1)pi/4'.

4 sin^3 t - 3 sin t = -(3 sin t - 4 sin^3 t) = -sin 3t, so f = 4 - sin 3theta with fundamental period 2pi/3; sympy's periodicity() returns 2*pi/3 and the other three candidates fail (max |f(t)-f(t+P)| = 1.94, 1.40, 1.94). The stem is truncated - it reads 'The periodic function ... is' while the options are periods, so it should read 'is periodic with period'.

53pi/5 - 10pi = 3pi/5, so cos(53pi/5) = cos(3pi/5) = -sin(pi/10) = -0.309017, and arcsin of that is -pi/10. sympy simplifies the whole expression to exactly -pi/10; options A and B (+/- 3pi/5 = 1.885) lie outside the arcsin range [-pi/2, pi/2] and C has the wrong sign.

Taking tan of both sides, (x+y+z-xyz)/(1-xy-yz-zx) = tan(pi) = 0, so x+y+z = xyz. Verified on three independent triples built by choosing x,y freely and solving z so the arctan sum is exactly pi: (2,3,1), (5,0.5,3.6667) and (1.3,4.7,1.17417) each give x+y+z - xyz = 0 to 1e-40. These are discriminating points because xyz there is 6, 9.167 and 7.174, so (xyz)^2 and 1/xyz are far away.

A line perpendicular to the x-axis is vertical, so it has the form x = constant, and passing through (-2, 9) fixes that constant at -2. Substituting (-2, 9) into each option, only C evaluates to 0 (A gives 7, B gives -4, D gives -11).

3x + y = 3 has slope -3, so the perpendicular has slope 1/3; through (2,2) that is y = x/3 + 4/3, giving a y-intercept of 4/3. sympy confirms the line passes through (2,2) and that the product of the two slopes is exactly -1.
